mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered events (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates expanding economic output and higher corporate revenue prospects, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in CPI inflation above 2% over the same quarter signals a real interest rate hike, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls below 102 (2% above 100 base) in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered quarters, or the median return is not statistically different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the previous 12-month average for five consecutive months signals a weakening housing market, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates population reclassification or labor force re-entry without job creation, which weakens labor market quality and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods.
